deglaciation.name: Ice-sheet retreat
deglaciation.desc: The Scandinavian ice sheet retreats from Pomerania. The Baltic basin still lies under the ice; the first ice-dammed lakes form at its front.

bil.name: Baltic Ice Lake
bil.desc: A lake dammed by the ice and the Øresund sill about 25 m above the ocean of the time. When the ice uncovers Mount Billingen the level drops by 25–28 m.

yoldia.name: Yoldia Sea
yoldia.desc: Connected to the ocean across central Sweden: first through the Billingen corridor, then the Närke strait. Salt water reaches the basin only around 11,700–11,100 cal BP.

ancylus.name: Ancylus Lake
ancylus.desc: Uplift closes the Swedish straits. The lake drains through the Svea River, later the Dana River through the Danish straits; the southern coast is drowned.

mastogloia.name: Mastogloia Sea
mastogloia.desc: The ocean rises faster than the Danish sills. Salt water advances slowly.

littorina.name: Littorina Sea
littorina.desc: Maximum transgression. Salinity clearly higher than today; the sea floods the southern lowlands while the Gulf of Bothnia emerges.

post-littorina.name: Limnaea and Mya Sea
post-littorina.desc: Shallowing of the Danish straits limits inflows. Salinity falls to the present level: about 7 PSU in the Baltic Proper.

billingen-before.label: Before the Billingen drainage
billingen-before.note: Ice still blocks the Billingen corridor. The lake drains through the Øresund.

billingen-after.label: After the Billingen drainage
billingen-after.note: The duration of the drainage is disputed: “1–2 years” is one estimate, not a consensus.

ancylus-max.label: Ancylus maximum
ancylus-max.note: Literature: level about +10 m above the ocean of the time.

ancylus-regression.label: Ancylus regression threshold
ancylus-regression.note: The outlet shifts from the Svea River to the Dana River.

littorina-onset.label: Onset of the Littorina transgression
littorina-onset.note: The ocean spills over the Darss sill.

littorina-max.label: Littorina maximum
littorina-max.note: Mid-Holocene highstand in the transition zones: 7.5–6.5 ka BP.

glossary: Calibrated years before 1950 (Present = 1950). Radiocarbon dates from the literature are converted with IntCal20; without it late-glacial dates shift by 1,000–1,500 years.
Land pressed down by the ice sheet slowly returns to equilibrium. Near Umeå it still rises about 10 mm a year; on the Polish coast hardly at all.
Global change of ocean level due to the water locked in ice sheets. 20,000 years ago the ocean stood about 120 m lower.
Relative sea level: where the water surface stood relative to the present land at a place. It combines isostasy and eustasy — hence H_paleo = H_now − RSL(t) with no separate eustatic term.
The lowest point between a basin and the ocean. In lake phases the sill, not the ocean, sets the Baltic water level.
Practical salinity unit, roughly grams of salt per kilogram of water. Ocean about 35, the Baltic Proper today about 7.
Heights measured against the sea surface of the time, not the present one. Only in this frame is a lake level (e.g. +25 m) one number for the whole basin.
Minimum and maximum ice extent (DATED-1) shown with the most credible outline.

about: This is a prototype, not a scientific result. Heights are real (GEBCO 2024 and the Steffen & Kaufmann 2025 RSL fields), but the pipeline does not have all its steps yet.
H_paleo = H_now − RSL(t) is computed in the browser, linear in time and bilinear in space — the same as the pipeline (agreement < 5 cm).

Water in the Baltic window is filled from the Skagerrak. When the basin has no connection to the ocean it fills up to its lowest outlet sill (priority-flood, ice acts as a wall) — the phase card compares that level with the literature, like the sill-check test (V-02).
Not yet included: the sill catalogue with elevations and states (C-05), salinity per basin (C-10), the eustatic curve (C-12), ice thickness (C-07) and data west of 0°E.
